newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela bolivar slumps on strong dlr demand.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela bolivar slumps on strong dlr demand.

text.p: The Venezuelan bolivar slumped in a day of volatile trade that saw the dollar soar to new heights until Central Bank intervention later firmed the rate to its final 483.25/484.25 per dollar close, traders said.
"It was very volatile. At one point the exchange rate hit 485 per dollar," said one trader.
Brokers reported strong corporate and interbank demand for dollars by a nervous market that sees recent gentle weakening of the bolivar as part of Central Bank moves to ease over-valuation.
Venezuela's foreign exchange market is unusual in that the Central Bank is its largest single supplier of dollars. Lately, however, the bank has hung back from the market.
"The Bank finally gave up ten days of passivity with some intervention at 485 bolivars per dollar," said one broker.
